description: During maintenance, a technician started opening a pipeline valve before confirming that the line was fully depressurized. No injury occurred.
Loose grating panel observed on walkway near separator bank B. Marked with warning tape; maintenance notified.
Contractor technician initiated flange bolting removal on an active export trunkline without verifying physical double-block-and-bleed status.
Rigging strap slipped off a 3-ton drill collar during offloading. The load swung violently through an unbarricaded gangway.
Cleaning crew opened manway of crude storage tank TK-104 and entered without completing atmospheric lower explosive limit (LEL) testing.
Electrician tested a 415V distribution board without wearing arc-flash face shield or voltage-rated gloves.
Mechanic removed the bleeder plug on pump P-201 suction line. Trapped condensate blew out under 18 bar pressure, narrowly missing face.
Overhead crane wire rope showed visible strand separation and bird-caging near the drum during pre-shift inspection.
Chemical tote storage area lacks proper secondary containment; minor glycol leak pooled on gravel foundation.
LOTO padlock placed on primary isolation valve, but isolation key remained in supervisor desk rather than being locked in group lockbox.
Oxy-acetylene cutting torch sparked 2 meters from an unsealed hydrocarbon sample drain. Fire watch was not equipped with a calibrated gas detector.
Shackle pin dropped from 12 meters height onto monkey board platform. Zone below had no dropped-object netting installed.
Pig receiver door swung open rapidly during opening procedure due to residual line pressure. Operator suffered bruised shoulder and minor cut.
Rigger unhooked 100% tie-off harness lanyard while transitioning across scaffolding transoms 8 meters above ground.
Pressure gauge PG-403 reading 0 bar while downstream bleeder valve was discovered plugged with wax and debris, masking live pressure.
Crane operator lifted casing bundle without a designated banksman/signaler visible in line of sight.
Eye wash and emergency shower station #4 found dry due to closed isolation supply valve.
Technician began loosening bolts on slug catcher manifold before performing isolation verification on nitrogen purge line.
Heavy transport driver observed reversing water bowser near flare knockout drum without ground guide or reverse alarm.
Webbing sling snapped during spool piece lift. Load fell 1.5m onto pipe rack, denting adjacent operational high-pressure lines.
Maintenance team relied on control room SCADA screen reading for line depressurization instead of physical vent check at the skid.
Standby person stepped away from vessel V-102 manway to fetch water while two contractors were active inside cleaning sand.
Contractor broke containment on fuel gas header filter housing without a signed positive isolation certificate.
Fire extinguisher placed at welding booth had expired hydrostatic pressure test certificate dated 2024.
Heavy subsea valve package swung over personnel during crane slew operation. Red barrier tape had been knocked down by wind.
Gas release detected by personal multigas monitor (25 ppm H2S) when technician unbolted blind flange on crude line. Isolation valve seat passing.
Wireline unit operator attempted to lubricate pack-off without bleeding stuffing box pressure to zero.
Oil seepage on compressor building stair treads created slippery footing condition.
Fitter disconnected hydraulic control line on shutdown valve SDV-101 before actuating manual bypass depressurization valve.
Crane load indicator calibration overdue by 60 days. Crane remained in routine heavy lifting service.
Depressurization hose disconnected violently during gas venting due to missing safety whip-check cable on pressurized connection.
Grinding spark shield not installed while performing weld prep near methanol injection skid tubing.
Scaffold toe-boards missing on platform level 3 adjacent to open drilling cellar pit.
Contractor technician bypassed the physical lockbox verification procedure, claiming supervisor verbal approval was granted over radio.
Tag line was not utilized on an 8m long structural beam lift; beam rotated into high-voltage lighting mast during moderate wind gusts.
Isolation spade installed backward with the open spacer facing flow stream during line break preparation, leaving line live.
Technician used uninsulated hand screwdrivers to terminate wires in energized junction box JB-12.
Continuous forced ventilation blower turned off during lunch break while personnel remained seated inside vessel bottom.
Mechanical fitter used a cheater bar on bleed needle valve, causing the stem packing to blow out and vent crude condensate mist.
Rig floor crew stood directly underneath suspended casing hanger while waiting for stabbing alignment.
Worker started opening valve V-204 without cross-checking the Energy Isolation Certificate tag numbers against P&ID schema.
Gas cylinders stored upright without safety retaining chains in open sun at ambient 44°C.
Trapped gas pocket ignited upon initial disc cutter contact on bypassed line due to inadequate nitrogen purging and residual gas verification.
Drop-zone safety barricading tape had fallen to deck and was trampled, leaving hazardous crane operating radius open to foot traffic.
Grinding work performed on flare line support structure without covering combustible cable trays 1.5m below with fire blanket.
Technician unbolted orifice plate flange while line was under 6 bar nitrogen pressure test; flange cracked open with loud hiss.
Contractor light pickup truck exceeded posted 20 km/h refinery speed limit, clocking 48 km/h near processing train.
Isolation verification checklist signed off in advance by junior technician prior to performing actual physical zero-pressure bleed checks.
Auxiliary winch hoist line caught on structural beam flange during crane swing, creating sudden jerk load on sling hook.
High pressure crude condensate sprayed out when valve packing gland was loosened without upstream line isolation confirmation.
Technician began unbolting flange on a transfer line without physically verifying the bleed valve was open and clear of wax.
Spilled lubricating oil found on the primary egress route from the compressor deck. Cleaned immediately.
During a dual-crane lift, a 5kg shackle fell from the rigging and landed 2 meters from a rigger. The exclusion zone was inadequate.
Maintenance crew applied LOTO locks but failed to perform a pressure bleed-down test before opening the strainer housing.
Welder started grinding operations without putting the fire blankets in place over nearby cable trays.
Temporary power cable routed across a wet walkway without proper elevation or cable ramps.
Residual pressure in a bypass line blew a blind flange off during removal. The line was isolated but not verified depressurized.
Warning barricades for a heavy lift were removed by a forklift driver and not replaced while the overhead lift was still active.
Gas tester only sampled the top of the separator vessel. Subsequent check found high LEL accumulation at the bottom before entry.
Operator assumed a block valve was holding pressure and skipped the double-block-and-bleed verification step.
Driver observed using a mobile phone while reversing a light utility vehicle in the main equipment yard.
A pipe joint swung unexpectedly due to wind, knocking over a scaffold tube. Tag lines were not being used.
Worker sustained minor facial cut when loosening a valve packing gland. Trapped fluid sprayed out. Isolation verification was bypassed.
Fire extinguisher at the muster point was found depressurized during routine safety walk.
Supervisor approved breaking containment based on control room gauge readings instead of requiring a local physical vent test.
Worker observed standing on the top rung of a step ladder to reach a junction box.
Dropped object: A wrench fell from a man basket during lifting, striking a worker on the hard hat. Drop zone was not barricaded.
Bleeder valve on the isolation manifold was found plugged with debris, making it impossible to verify zero energy.
Pressure gauge failed during wireline operations. Operator nearly unlatched the lubricator while it was still pressurized.
Fitter used a non-sparking hammer to loosen a flange without first confirming the permit-to-work isolation checklist was completed.
Crane operator lifted a load while a roustabout was still standing directly underneath adjusting the slings.
Pallet of chemical drums stacked unevenly and leaning heavily toward the pedestrian walkway.
Loud hiss and gas release when cracking a flange. The primary isolation valve was leaking through. Bleeder had not been left open.
Standby person left the entrance of the vessel to go to the bathroom while two workers were still inside.
Sling found with severe abrasion damage during pre-use inspection. Sling was removed from service.
Contractor proceeded with dismantling a pump casing. LOTO was applied, but isolation verification was marked 'N/A' on the permit.
Worker tripped on an unsecured cable tray cover and sprained their ankle.
A plug blew out of a high-pressure line during maintenance. The team failed to vent the line locally before starting work.
Crane slew brake slipped, causing a suspended load to drift over an active walkway that had not been barricaded off.
Gas test for hot work permit was conducted an hour before work actually commenced, invalidating the atmospheric clearance.
Technician unbolted a spectacle blind without checking if the upstream line had been purged with nitrogen.
Electrical panel door left wide open and unattended in a dusty environment.
Banksman was guiding the crane operator while standing between the suspended load and a solid steel bulkhead. Line of fire violation.
Sudden release of crude oil when loosening a flange. The wrong valve was locked out due to incorrect tagging on the P&ID.
Forklift tynes observed to have deep gouges and cracks near the heel.
Maintenance team skipped the zero-energy verification step because they were running behind schedule on a critical path shutdown task.
A synthetic sling parted during a lift. The load dropped 1 meter. Barricades were up, so no personnel were in the danger zone.
Worker observed not wearing hearing protection while walking through the high-noise compressor housing area.
Worker suffered a contusion when a trapped pocket of pressurized gas blew a blind flange into their chest. Isolation was not verified.
Entrants failed to sign the entry log board before entering the vessel.
Wind speeds exceeded safe lifting parameters, but lifting operations were not paused by the lifting supervisor.
Operator used an unauthorized homemade key to open an isolation valve because the official LOTO key was lost.
Reverse alarm on a vacuum truck was found to be inoperable during pre-start checks.
During flange parting, hydrocarbon vapor was released. The line was isolated, but the physical verification to ensure depressurization was not conducted.
Sparks from cutting operations fell to the deck below. Fire watcher was assigned but had left the area to get welding rods.
A loosely secured wooden beam fell from a lifted cargo basket, landing in an unbarricaded zone near the tool shack.
Fitter proceeded with breaking containment without confirming the bleed valve was open, risking exposure to trapped pressure.
Safety shower pull-rod handle was broken off, rendering it unusable.
Technician experienced a near-asphyxiation event when a supposedly isolated nitrogen purge line vented in their face. Isolation verification failed.
Rig crew used standard barrier tape instead of hard physical barricades for a heavy lift operation drop zone.
Entrant's personal multi-gas detector was found turned off while working inside the vessel.
Team leader signed the positive isolation certificate without personally witnessing the depressurization check.
Scaffolding tag indicated 'Do Not Use', but workers were seen placing tools on the platform.
Dropped object. A D-ring dropped from a load being lifted over a walkway. The walkway had not been properly closed off.
High-pressure water blasted out of a drain point when opened. The isolation valve was passing. The crew failed to check the pressure gauge first.
Combustible trash bins were not removed from the welding area prior to starting hot work.
Technician isolated the breaker but did not apply a personal lock, relying only on a generic warning tag.
Isolation bleed valve handle was stripped, making it impossible to confidently verify the line was depressurized.
Workers observed ducking under active crane lift warning barricades to take a shortcut to the mess hall.
Maintenance bypassed the isolation verification test, assuming the line was empty because it had been out of service for two weeks.
Poor illumination in the pump house basement area. Several bulbs burnt out.
Technician sprayed with residual chemical during filter changeout. The vent valve was blocked with debris, and zero-energy was not confirmed.
Forklift operator transporting a load that obstructed forward vision without using a spotter.
A pipe clamp fell from height. The area below had no red warning tape or hard barricades to prevent entry.
Operator cracked a flange to vent pressure instead of using the designated bleed valve, creating an uncontrolled release path.
Fire watcher observed reading a phone instead of monitoring the cutting sparks.
Shelving unit in the warehouse was heavily overloaded and bowing in the center.
Valve bonnet blew off when unbolted due to trapped upstream pressure. The isolation verification was pencil-whipped on the permit.
Rigger attempted to manually stop a swinging load instead of using the attached tag line.
Crew started work based on an old isolation certificate from the previous day without re-verifying isolation status.
Worker entered the skirt of a vessel without a confined space permit, claiming it was 'just to retrieve a dropped wrench.'
Hole in grating on the upper deck was left uncovered and unbarricaded.
A tool bag fell from the derrick. The drill floor drop zone was not properly secured with barricades.
Technician failed to check the pressure gauge on the bypass loop before removing a block valve. Isolation verification skipped.
Contractor observed running down a flight of metal stairs without maintaining three points of contact.
Operator did not re-verify zero pressure after a shift handover before breaking wireline connections.
Line snapped back forcefully when flange bolts were removed. Pressure was still present due to lack of verification.
Crane anti-two-block warning device was malfunctioning.
Worker attempted to reset a tripped 480V breaker without investigating the cause of the trip first.
Crew broke containment on a flare line. The permit was issued, but physical venting and isolation verification were not performed.
First aid kit at the main workshop missing eye wash saline solution.
Isolation was put in place by night shift. Day shift assumed it was correct and proceeded without their own verification.
Crane lifted a load directly over the heads of two workers who ignored the drop zone barricades.
Worker improperly lifting a 25kg chemical bag using their back instead of legs.
Unexpected spray of pressurized fluid from a drain point. The operator opened it without checking the isolation status upstream.
Welding machine grounding cable was frayed, exposing bare wire.
Permit required physical verification of zero energy, but the technician just signed it off at the supervisor desk.
A bolt dropped 15m from a derrick, hitting a worker's arm. The area was not properly barricaded to prevent access.
Site speed limit sign at the main entrance faded and unreadable.
Fitter broke containment on a live line. LOTO was planned but not physically executed or verified.
Rescue harness was not worn by the entrant when going into the storage tank.
Flange separation resulted in a loud pop and release of pressure. Isolation verification was bypassed.
Rigger signaled to hoist without checking if the load path was clear of obstacles.
Harness lanyard shock absorber found deployed during inspection, indicating previous fall. Still in use.
Supervisor hurried the crew, instructing them to skip the physical bleed check and just look at the panel gauge.
Slag from cutting torch ignited dry grass near the fence line. Fire watch extinguished it immediately.
Chain block failed under load. The engine block dropped 2 feet. The area was unbarricaded.
Employee wearing loose jewelry while working near rotating pump shafts.
Pressurized gas vented forcefully when a blinded flange was unbolted without isolation verification. Worker suffered ear drum pain.
Barricades around a heavy lift zone were blown over by wind and no personnel were assigned to replace them.
Technician broke containment on a bypass valve without performing a physical zero-energy check on the bleeder.
Puddle of hydraulic fluid found near forklift parking bay. Slip hazard.
Crane lifted a heavy skid over an active walkway. Drop zone was not barricaded, exposing passing workers.
LOTO applied, but supervisor authorized opening the line without verifying line depressurization.
Welder failed to clear oily rags from the immediate vicinity before sparking the torch.
Loud release of gas when unbolting a flange. Isolation was passing and not verified by the crew.
Hard barricades were removed to allow a truck to pass and never replaced during active lifting.

Ventilation blower failed, but entrants were not immediately evacuated from the tank.

A 2kg shackle dropped from the derrick. Warning tape was blown away, and a worker was standing nearby.
